## Moments and vanishing

**Topic scope:** Generalized vanishing, Gaussian moments and Image/Mathieu spaces.

**Computed obligation progress:** 38 open; 1 proved / discharged.

**Authored scope assessment:** The universal GVC/GMC dimension classifications and Gaussian dimension-degree boundary are claimed closed in their exact domains. Higher-dimensional GMC is refuted by witnesses; general Gaussian extensions is not an unrestricted open GMC claim.

**Authored scope assessment:** Safety-to-purity is the converse implication to GMC. Its primitive-vacuum equivalence is represented in one direction with equivalence metadata to preserve acyclicity.

**Authored scope assessment:** Two-base marker generation supplies a proved reduction, while purity-to-base-marker polynomiality remains a mathematical gap.

**Authored scope assessment:** The full sixteen-parameter two-pair cubic Image stratum is positive with sharp mixed cutoff m>3 deg_z Q. Constant-profile extraction uses a proper holomorphic-volume V-filtration argument and explicit boundary resolutions; the exact eleven-parameter certificate finishes all exceptional cases. The least failing bihomogeneous balanced degree is four. Independent review remains pending.

**Authored scope assessment:** The latest two-pair Image cubic note now supplies an internal full(3,3) proof and sharp minimum balanced degree4. Its prior F1-versus-closing-gap inconsistency is obsolete; external review/formal coverage remain separate.

**Authored scope assessment:** Theorem 5.5 extends the retained primitive Image family to every even balanced degree d>=4. Odd height powers are allowed: for odd k the fixed marker survives at every even m, which already violates eventual mixed vanishing. The next primitive frontier is odd degree five, with F mod R nonzero required from the start; invariant padding cannot settle it. This internal deduction has no independent review, formal verification or novelty claim; unrestricted Image failure was already known in the retained results.

**Authored scope assessment:** The real signed-height one-affine-profile class is classified: q=r gives primitive failures only in even minimal degree, while q<r is safe for all original multipliers. A separate four-moment certificate excludes every bilinear multiple of the retained quartic from primitive degree five. Neither restriction decides arbitrary primitive odd degree five. The DAG separates angular identities, the contraction bridge, primitivity, Image membership, quartic specialization and padding. The full geometric nullcone interpretation retains a definition/application audit obligation.

### GAUSSIAN-H21-AFFINE-CHART

[Gaussian H(2,1): affine charts, radial phases and obstructions](moments/vanishing/GAUSSIAN_AFFINE_ISOTROPIC_CHART.md)

**Exact scope:** Complete all-degree purity classification for Wh(Z)+v(Z)Y^2+b(Z)Y+k(Z), with explicit safe marker cutoffs and no nonisotropic constant-fibre axis for its unsafe branch. For B=c(Z)W+u(Z), g=Wh(Z)+k(Z), all pure members are safe if deg c<=8, with unrestricted h,u,k. More generally, for nonconstant c whose root multiplicities are at most two, purity is equivalent to a=0, h,c divisible by Z^2, u,k divisible by Z. Thus nonconstant squarefree c of arbitrary degree has no pure members. For arbitrary multiplicities nonconstant c excludes purity when a!=0; unshared roots of c,h also have no multiplicity restriction. The same positive-weight classification holds if ord h>=ord c at every common root, including the entire c|h subfamily, without multiplicity bounds. The sharp four-level argument classifies the mixed family whenever every nonzero common root avoids ceil(2m/3)<=ord h<=m-3, m=ord c>=9. Polynomial cubic barriers realize nonpositive volume order at every pair in that strip but are not pure. For a nonzero constant lambda, every pure phase lambda W^2+Wh(Z)+c(Z)WY+aY^2+u(Z)Y+k(Z) is quadratic; nonconstant c(Z) admits no pure member, by a connected double-cover period argument retaining positive-genus cycles. For polynomial ell(Z) of degree at least two in place of lambda, no pure member exists when gcd(ell,c^2) has only simple/double roots and the explicit fixed and moving determinant sources are clean. Moving cleanliness is automatic unless ell/gcd(ell,c^2) is constant or proportional to Z. In particular gcd(ell,c)=1 admits no pure member, without multiplicity bounds. When c=0, no pure member exists if ell has only simple/double roots and ell(0)!=0 or h(0)!=0. Acyclicity on the determinant or reduced-root divisor proves that localization preserves the original seed. If the sole unclean fixed source is a simple origin under the stated volume hypotheses, a rank-one actual Gysin-kernel argument forces a=u(0)=k(0)=0 for purity. For every integer nu>=1 and every complex polynomial k, Z^(2nu+1)W^2+Z^nu WY-W/2+k(Z) is not pure: an exact all-order marked kernel and uniform factorial coefficient bound treat this moving-nullsource-zero branch directly. Analytic amplitudes extend it to all constant a and u divisible by Z^nu. More generally the entire R=0 branch e=ell/gcd(ell,c^2)=kappa Z with c(0)=0 admits no pure member, for arbitrary u,k and root multiplicities. An exact actual Wick-residue/Lagrange kernel, selected-sheet continuation and uniform contour coefficient bound prove this without localization at the degenerate moving source. The six-parameter family alpha Z^3+beta W^3+gamma Z^2 W Y+delta Z W^2 Y+e((ZW)^2-2)+eta(Y^2-1) is pure exactly when e=eta=0 and one angular coefficient pair vanishes; moments 2,3,4,5,6,8 force this all-order safe form. Every all-degree radial phase aY^2+B(ZW)Y+g(ZW) is pure only if it is zero, using a relative endpoint module of rank D and a complete endpoint period pairing. Consequently weakly one-sided angular support is safe in all degrees, with cutoff m>deg Q. A fixed-multipuncture logarithmic seed estimate and an ordinary-volume estimate at double roots supply these extensions, using the stated comparison dependencies. No polynomial automorphism preserving 2ZW+Y^2 sends Long's quartic into H(2,1). General H(2,1) remains open.

### IMAGE2-EVEN-PRIMITIVE

[All even primitive two-pair Image degrees](foundations/extended-geometry/TWO_PAIR_IMAGE_MATHIEU_COUNTEREXAMPLE.md)

**Exact scope:** For every characteristic-zero field and integer k>=0, F_k=T^k(R+Z)^(k+1)(2WR^2-2RT^2-ZT^2) has balanced bidegree (d,d), d=2k+4. For every m>=1, E2(F_k^m)=0; E2(ZF_k^m)=(dm+2)! integral_0^1 w^(km)(1-w^2)^m dw is a nonzero rational scalar when km is even, and is zero when km is odd. R does not divide F_k and F_k is not a proper power, even up to a nonzero scalar. Thus every even balanced degree d>=4 has a primitive, non-proper-power Image witness with fixed marker Z; no primitive odd-degree result is asserted.

**Authored state:** proved. **Graph state:** proved. **Dependency coverage:** partial.

### HOPF-REAL-HEIGHT-PROFILES

[Real signed-height affine-profile classification](foundations/extended-geometry/HOPF_LIFT_CLASSIFICATION.md)

**Exact scope:** On the real Hopf sphere let p=gamma x^(-r)(1+x)^q P(t(1+x)), where r,q>=1 are integers, gamma is real nonzero, P is a nonzero real polynomial, and (1-w^2)^r divides P. All pure sphere moments vanish iff q<=r. At q=r marker x survives every even power; at q<r every fixed polynomial marker is eventually zero. For n=deg(P) the minimal balanced lift has degree d=2n+q-r and is R-primitive. At q=r it is an Image failure of even balanced degree 2n. At q<r the original Image conclusion holds for every fixed multiplier, including unbalanced multipliers; m>=2 deg_z(Q)+1 suffices. This class allows mixed signed-height powers but only one affine phase profile with real coefficients; no complex-profile or arbitrary primitive odd-degree classification is asserted.

**Authored state:** proved. **Graph state:** proved. **Dependency coverage:** partial.

**Recorded assurances:** Independent replay: not recorded; Formal verification: not recorded; External review: not recorded.

### TWO-PAIR-IMAGE-CUBIC

[Complete cubic two-pair Image positivity and sharp balanced degree four](foundations/extended-geometry/TWO_PAIR_IMAGE_CUBIC_STRATIFICATION.md)

**Exact scope:** For every characteristic-zero field and every bihomogeneous F of bidegree (3,3), vanishing E2(F^m) for all m>=1 implies E2(QF^m)=0 for every polynomial Q whenever m>3 deg_z Q. The coefficient three is sharp. Over C, every pure sphere cubic is orthogonally and scalar equivalent to a strictly one-sided phase or y+xt-x^3/2. Together with the quartic counterexample, the least failing bihomogeneous balanced degree is four.

## Jacobian and Keller maps

**Topic scope:** Polynomial Keller maps, their fibres, monodromy and boundary geometry.

**Computed obligation progress:** 15 open.

Retained ordinary characteristic-zero polynomial Keller constructions have determinant one and explicit collisions; their internal consequence is failure of the unrestricted Jacobian conjecture. The earlier full-JC-open summary was inconsistent with these source claims. This is internal assurance, not external acceptance.

JC2 remains a separate unresolved target. Ruling degree, generic map degree, graph degree and sparse support minima are distinct quantities.

A canonical non-atomic vector-bundle receiver already exists. Canonical atomic coupling remains open; an automorphism-invariant natural fixed frame is obstructed, not an unqualified existence gap.

| JAC-MONODROMY-S1 | claim | proved / partial | In the exact setting/notation of JAC-MONODROMY, the named sub-result states:  Work first over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic zero. A Keller map is a polynomial morphism F:X=A^m -> Y=A^m with det DF in k*. It is dominant, generically finite and etale. Write  \[  K=k(Y),\quad L=k(X),\quad M=\text{Galois closure of }L/K,\qquad  G=\operatorname{Gal}(M/K),\quad H=\operatorname{Gal}(M/L). \]  The degree is n=[L:K]=[G:H]. Analytic continuation over C, or the geometric etale fundamental group in general, acts on the cosets G/H. This is the monodromy action. It is faithful because M is the Galois closure.  The action must be recorded together with H. The deck group of the generic cover is N_G(H)/H, equivalently the centralizer of G in S_n. It need not equal G. Polynomial source symmetries covering target symmetries form yet another object. These three meanings of "symmetry group" must be kept separate.  For a nonclosed ground field, geometric and arithmetic monodromy are different groups, G_geom normal in G_arith <= S_n. Their quotient describes the algebraic constant field of the Galois closure. The F11 example below makes this distinction necessary, even with an explicit rational formula.  The absolute spectrum consists of actions realized by polynomial Keller self-maps of affine space, allowing dimension to vary. The chart spectrum allows smooth affine source and target varieties and a chosen volume form. A field-versal spectrum additionally asks to realize all torsors of a specified action. These are different problems. | [jacobian/monodromy-theory/THEORY.md](jacobian/monodromy-theory/THEORY.md): Section 1. The object being classified |

| JAC-MONODROMY-S3 | claim | proved / partial | In the exact setting/notation of JAC-MONODROMY, the named sub-result states:  **Lemma.** Let F:A^m -> A^m be Keller over k. For every prime divisor D=V(q) in the target there is a prime divisor E in the source dominating D, and its ramification index in L/K is one.  Indeed q(F) is nonconstant, since F is dominant. A nonconstant polynomial over an algebraically closed field is not a unit and has a prime factor. Every component E of V(q(F)) has dimension m-1. The restriction of a quasi-finite morphism is quasi-finite, so its image has dimension m-1; its image closure is D. At the generic points the local rings are DVRs. The local map is etale, hence has ramification index one and separable residue extension. This works for m=1 as well.  In fact q(F) is squarefree: every component just considered has index one. Distinct target prime divisors have disjoint sets of source prime-divisor factors, since such a factor cannot dominate two different divisors. Consequently pullback on the free divisor groups is a primitive injection: each target prime maps to a nonempty sum of distinct source primes, and the supports of these sums are disjoint. Choosing one source prime over each target prime gives a splitting. The cokernel is free.  One elementary consequence, useful for quadratic resolvents, is  \[  b(F)\in k(X)^{*d}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad  b\in k(Y)^{*d}\qquad(d\ge2).  \tag{3.1} \]  Write the divisor of b in target prime divisors and compare valuations on one source prime over each. Every exponent must be divisible by d; the remaining constant is a d-th power in algebraically closed k. This argument needs neither a prescribed primitive polynomial nor a Jacobian ansatz. It cannot be applied to a selected target slice instead of the whole affine target. | [jacobian/monodromy-theory/THEORY.md](jacobian/monodromy-theory/THEORY.md): Section 3. Every affine divisor is met without ramification |

Consequently  \[  \boxed{\langle gHg^{-1}:g\in G\rangle=G.}  \tag{4.1} \]  Here "geometric inertia" means inertia after strict henselization at D; it is cyclic in residue characteristic zero. The group is determined up to conjugacy. The theorem concerns divisors of A^m, not arbitrary divisors at infinity on a compactification.  To prove the first assertion, use E from Section 3. In the standard inertia action on embeddings of L into M, the orbits have sizes equal to ramification indices of geometric branches. Index one gives a fixed sheet. Equivalently, for a suitable conjugate of H one has I_D <= gHg^-1. An unramified branch may have a nontrivial residue-field extension before strict henselization; this does not remove its inertia fixed points.  For the second assertion, let N be the normal subgroup generated by all the I_D, and normalize Y in M^N. This normalization is finite, since Y is excellent and M^N/K is finite. All codimension-one inertia is killed, so the finite morphism is unramified in codimension one. Its source is normal and its target regular. Purity of the branch locus makes it finite etale everywhere. Affine space over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field has no nontrivial connected finite etale cover. Thus M^N=K and N=G. Equivalence between algebraic finite etale covers and finite analytic covers is the Riemann-existence comparison of SGA 1, Expose XII, Theorem 5.1 and Corollary 5.2. | JAC-STRUCTURE-S1 | claim | proved / partial | In the exact setting/notation of JAC-STRUCTURE, the named sub-result states:  **UAQTILT1.** Let K be any field of characteristic other than two, let h in K[S] have degree N>=3 and h'(0)!=0, and let B,C be independent indeterminates. Then \[  h(S)+BS^2-C  \tag{1} \] has arithmetic and geometric Galois group S_N over K(B,C). Here geometric means after extending K to an algebraic closure; B and C remain variables. There is no restriction involving N, N-1, or the characteristic dividing N.  Cohen's 1980 Theorem 1 proves this immediately. In odd characteristic p, the functions 1,S^2,h(S) are linearly independent over K(S^p): the nonzero S coefficient of h gives a nonzero residue-one component, distinct from residues zero and two. His 1981 correction explicitly preserves Theorem 1. We give a direct proof to expose exactly where odd characteristic matters.  Extend K to an algebraic closure. The polynomial (1) is irreducible and separable: it is linear in the independent C, and its S derivative has nonzero constant term h'(0).  For double transitivity, divide the two-root equation by the diagonal: \[  A(X,Y)+B(X+Y)=0,\qquad  A(X,Y)=\frac{h(X)-h(Y)}{X-Y}.                         \tag{2} \] The irreducible polynomial X+Y does not divide A, because \[  A(X,-X)=\frac{h(X)-h(-X)}{2X} \] has nonzero constant term h'(0). Thus (2), viewed as a polynomial linear in B, is primitive and irreducible in K[X,Y,B]. It stays irreducible over K(B). Localizing away from X=Y gives the integral incidence of two distinct roots of the generic fibre; its projection to C is dominant. Equivalently the point stabilizer is transitive on the other roots. The monodromy is doubly transitive.  There is also a transposition. A critical point r is nonzero and satisfies \[  B(r)=-\frac{h'(r)}{2r},\qquad  C(r)=h(r)-\frac{rh'(r)}2.                           \tag{3} \] The rational function B(r) has a simple pole at zero, so B'(r) is not identically zero in any odd characteristic. The extension K(r)/K(B(r)) is finite separable. Differentiation with respect to B preserves its intermediate field K(B(r),C(r)); the identity \[  \frac{dC}{dB}=r^2                                  \tag{4} \] therefore places r^2 in that field. But B(r) is not in K(r^2), since every pole at zero of a function of r^2 has even order. As K(r)/K(r^2) is quadratic, this proves \[  K(B(r),C(r))=K(r).                                 \tag{5} \] The critical-value curve is birationally parametrized by r. | [jacobian/universal-keller-structure/PROOF.md](jacobian/universal-keller-structure/PROOF.md): Section 1. A quadratic-tilt lemma in every odd characteristic |

When the map extends polynomially, it is absolutely and stably atomic under polynomial composition. This includes the exceptional negative profiles in odd characteristic. The seed-free map has the same assertions with degree three.  Indeed over K=k(pi) the complete generic fibre has equation \[  E(S)=h(S)+bS^2-c/2,\qquad  h(S)=S+\pi S^3+\sum_{j=4}^N f_j(\pi)\pi^jS^j.        \tag{6} \] Here h'(0)=1 and deg h=N. For clarity, the atomicity step is characteristic-free. A polynomial factorization of a Keller map has Keller factors by the chain rule and the fact that polynomial-ring units are constants. A primitive generic permutation action admits no proper intermediate field, so one factor has generic degree one. An etale birational self-map of affine space is an open immersion by Zariski's Main Theorem. Its complement has no divisor, since such a divisor would restrict to a nonconstant unit on the source; normal Hartogs extension and affineness then make the immersion an isomorphism. Thus the degree-one factor is an automorphism. **Topic scope:** Factorial moment functionals, composition rigidity and Strong Factorial families.

**Computed obligation progress:** 20 open.

Unrestricted FC and SFC remain open. Universal special-family theorems do not supply an arbitrary-support reduction.

The pencil and coupled-family descriptions retain the scale, Gamma-shape, block and ordinary coefficient-ring normalization restrictions stated in their proofs.

Higher-gap rank and backward-pivot results are proved criteria. Uniform actual-family rank/nonzero-pivot assertions remain open; finite controls do not discharge them. Priority and independent review are separate obligations.

New gap-three certificates cover entire infinite matrices for n=2..16 and all beta>=0; initial minors and pivots have separate unbounded-index scopes. Prime-power terminal families and arbitrary-support initial pairs do not close all univariate binomial SFC.

Effective large-gap and large-lower-exponent bounds reduce each fixed ordinary terminal order to an explicit finite support rectangle; all rectangles as N varies are still unchecked. Fixed-shape auxiliary positive networks do not yet transfer through the signed cyclic Wronskian map.

All lower exponents and gaps are separated through terminal five for ordinary factorials and through terminal four for every positive Gamma shape. Arithmetic criteria, all-j root-scale monotonicity and the diagonal derivative embedding do not discharge the remaining all-N>=6 rectangles or uniform gap-three H3 total nonnegativity.

A uniform all-gap identity now normalizes the moment discriminant as an (n-1)-square cyclic Hurwitz determinant. Its nonnegativity is proved for every positive shape, giving the last three gap-three special minors nonnegative at all indices. Strictness and the remaining intermediate minors are open.

### BINOMIAL-ARITHMETIC-STARTS

[Arithmetic terminal criteria and a resultant stability obstruction](factorial/image-rigidity/ARITHMETIC_FRONTIER_TERMINAL_ORDERS.tex)

The common-quotient criterion requires floor(aN/d)=floor(a(N-1)/d)=q and q+N<p. [All-gap discriminants, cyclic Hurwitz minors and auxiliary factorizations](factorial/image-rigidity/gap_three_hurwitz_structure.tex)

### Topic obligations

- **FACTORIAL-GENERAL-FC** (mathematical; open): Unrestricted higher-dimensional Factorial conjecture beyond the stated proven families.
- **FACTORIAL-LOWER-ONE-HIGHER-GAP** (mathematical; open): Close the specified X(A+B X^d) families for all indices and positive Gamma shapes at d>=3.
- **GAP-FACTORIAL-3** (verification; open): Independent mathematical and priority review.
- **FACTORIAL-GENERAL-SFC** (mathematical; open): Strong Factorial for arbitrary nonzero polynomial supports with correct term-count windows, beyond listed families.
- **FACTORIAL-GAP-FULL-RANK** (mathematical; open): For the actual positive Gamma moment family at higher gaps, prove all (d-1)-minors have no common nonzero root uniformly in the stated index/shape range.
- **FACTORIAL-GAP3-PIVOTS** (mathematical; open): Every pivot in the backward certificate for actual W_r/W_r(0) in physical gamma=n+beta-1,beta>0 is nonzero.
- **FACTORIAL-GAP3-HURWITZ-TN** (mathematical; open): Prove that the whole infinite H3(W_(n,n+beta-1)) is totally nonnegative for every integer n>=2 and every beta>0; the n<=16 theorem and first nine pivots do not prove this.
- **FACTORIAL-GAP3-STAIRCASE-POSITIVITY** (mathematical; open): For every p>=1, r=ceil(p/2), prove the special minor Delta_p(x+r,beta) has nonnegative rational coefficients and a positive constant. Delta_p=det(C_(3j-i)), rows i=k..k+r-1, columns j=1..r, k=2r-p+1. Retained certificates prove p<=8 only.
- **FACTORIAL-GAP3-ALL-PAIRS** (mathematical; open): For every beta>0, nonzero X(A+B X^3), and terminal N>=2, the Gamma moments at N-1 and N cannot both vanish. The ordinary quartic-binomial case is beta=1.
- **FACTORIAL-BINOMIAL-RECTANGLE-PAIRS** (mathematical; open): For every integer N>=6 and all integers1<=a<A_N,2<=d<D_N, prove gcd_Qt (source reference: `M_(N-1,a,d`),M_(N,a,d))=1, where D_N=2(N-1)*min{e:2^e>=4N(N-1)} and A_N=(N*D_N^2+D_N)(4N+1)^N. Each rectangle is finite; infinitely many N remain unverified. Ordinary terminal<=5 is proved separately.
- **FACTORIAL-ALL-UNIVARIATE-BINOMIAL-SFC** (mathematical; open): For every integers a>=0,d>=1,N>=2, the ordinary factorial moment polynomials M_(N-1,a,d) and M_(N,a,d) are coprime, equivalently every nonzero complex X^a(A+B X^d) has a nonzero moment in every consecutive positive pair. Neither all-index lower-one gap-three nor unrestricted lower exponents are presumed solved.
- **GAP-BINOMIAL-FINITE-RECTANGLES** (mathematical; open): For every remaining ordinary terminal N>=6, verify consecutive coprimality inside the explicit support rectangle. All ordinary terminal orders<=5 are proved, while arbitrary positive Gamma shapes are proved through terminal4 only; rectangle sizes depend on N.
- **GAP-BINOMIAL-PARAMETER-OBSTRUCTIONS** (mathematical; open): Exclude simultaneous finite obstruction conditions for the unique polynomial solution of the order-(d+1) parameter recurrence in the uncovered range.
- **GAP-ALL-EXPONENTS-SQUAREFREE** (mathematical; open): Prove individual squarefreeness of all factorial binomial polynomials in the remaining finite-candidate exponent range; all-indexSFC alone does not prove individual squarefreeness.
- **GOAL-ORDINARY-BINOMIAL-SFC** (mathematical; open): For every integer lower exponent a>=0 and gap d>=1, every nonzero complex phase X^a(A+B X^d) has no two consecutive zero ordinary factorial moments at any starting index; this does not assert arbitrary Gamma shape or arbitrary polynomial support.
- **FACTORIAL-BINOMIAL-DIAGONAL-PAIRS** (mathematical; open): For every integers a,d>=1,N>=2, prove coprimality of D^((a-1)N)S_(aN) and D^((a-1)(N-1))S_(a(N-1)), where S_m(z)=sum_k binom(m,k)(m+1)_(dk)z^(m-k). The ordinary positive-lower-exponent binomial assertion is exactly this diagonal statement. Simplicity, stability and base consecutive coprimality alone are insufficient, as the explicit generic counterexample shows.
- **GAP-POSITIVE-GAMMA-TERMINAL-FIVE** (mathematical; open): For every positive Gamma shape beta,integer lower exponent a>=0 and gap d>=1,prove that each nonzero complex X^a(A+B X^d) has a nonzero moment in orders4or5,or give a counterexample in this exact powered-Gamma family. Ordinary beta=1 is now proved;the positive finite-Gamma-convolution counterexample is outside this family.
- **GOAL-UNSHIFTED-RESULTANT-COEFFICIENT-POSITIVITY** (mathematical; open): For every integers N>=2,d>=1,prove that all coefficients in a of R_(N,d)(a) are nonnegative. Together with its strictly positive leading coefficient this makes R_(N,d)(a)>0 for every real a>0. The fixed N=8,d=5 obstruction to Hurwitz stability has strictly positive coefficients and does not obstruct this weaker target.
- **FACTORIAL-LOWER-ONE-TERMINAL-DETERMINANT** (mathematical; open): For every integers n>=2,d>=3 and every beta>0, prove D_(n,d)(n+beta-1)>0, with D the (n-1)-square determinant in thm:discriminant. Nonnegativity is now proved. By the exact discriminant identity and the two-moment bridge, strictness is equivalent to all-index lower-one positive-Gamma SFC at these gaps.
- **FACTORIAL-GAP3-TERMINAL-MINOR-STRICT** (mathematical; open): For every integer n>=2 and beta>0, prove Delta_(2n-2)(W_(n,n+beta-1))>0. This determinant and the next two special minors are already nonnegative uniformly. Strictness is equivalent to simplicity of the coupled moment polynomial and suffices for the gap-three lower-one Gamma family; it does not assert all H3 minors are nonnegative.

## Dixmier and Weyl algebras

**Topic scope:** Formal Weyl-algebra lifts, finite scalar mates and centralizers.

**Computed obligation progress:** 13 open.

All-order formal lifting has polynomial coefficients, but supplies no common finite spatial-degree bound. Evaluation of an unbounded h-adic series at one is unavailable.

A proved bounded-realization criterion would produce a finite nonsurjective Weyl endomorphism from the specified noninvertible classical frame and common degree bound; that bound is not supplied.

The scalar finite-mate classification is for the fixed pure form and actual finite operators. Mixed/nonscalar carriers and actual Long centralizer/radical inputs remain outside it; DC1 and DC2 remain unresolved.

### DIXMIER-FORMAL-LIFTING

[Formal quantum lifting and the finite-degree realization criterion](dixmier/dixmier-formal-lifting/PROOF.md)

**Exact scope:** Every char0 polynomial symplectic full frame has all-order formal Weyl/Moyal lift with polynomial coefficients. One common finite spatial degree bound for a lift of a noninvertible classical map implies nonsurjective finite A_n(C) endomorphism.

| DIX-QDI1-S1 | claim | proved / partial | In the exact setting/notation of DIX-QDI1, the named sub-result states:  Let K have characteristic zero, F=K((h)), and let A be the finite PBW algebra over F on n canonical pairs, with [p_i,x_j]=h*delta_ij and the other generator commutators zero. It is multiplicative: normalized nonzero factors reduce to nonzero commutative polynomials, because every commutator is divisible by h. Hence v extends to Q, with value group Z, central uniformizer h, and residue field \[                    \overline Q=K(x_1,\ldots,x_n,p_1,\ldots,p_n).                                                                \tag{1} \] Indeed every rational function in the commuting residue variables is the residue of a fraction of finite PBW polynomials. Let Qhat be the valuation completion; it remains a division ring, with this residue field. The usual geometric-series inverse proves the division claim.  Let psi be a polynomial symplectic endomorphism of affine 2n-space. Its Jacobian is a unit, so its coordinate functions are algebraically independent and the induced function-field extension is finite. Put \[  \delta=[K(x,p):K(\psi(x,p))]. \] Let Phi be any full formal lift of psi, with polynomial coefficients at each h order, as in [QFL1](dixmier/dixmier-formal-lifting/PROOF.md). Its images belong to Qhat even if their spatial degrees are unbounded. A finite source PBW polynomial with its least scalar valuation removed has a nonzero classical polynomial reduction; its image reduces to that polynomial evaluated at psi, which is nonzero. Thus substitution preserves valuation.  It follows that Phi embeds the source Weyl division ring into Qhat and extends isometrically to its completion. Denote the resulting complete image by Ehat. Its residue field is exactly K(psi(x,p)). When Phi has common finite spatial support, its images lie in A over F; write E=Phi(Q) inside Q. In that case Ehat is also the completion of this uncompleted image division ring. Without finite support we do not claim E is a subring of Q. | [dixmier/dixmier-formal-lifting/QUANTUM_DIVISION_AND_COMPLETION.md](dixmier/dixmier-formal-lifting/QUANTUM_DIVISION_AND_COMPLETION.md): Section Valuations on the quantum rational function fields |
| DIX-QDI1-S2 | claim | proved / partial | In the exact setting/notation of DIX-QDI1, the named sub-result states:  Here is the general valued-division-ring statement used throughout. If their residue extension has finite degree delta, then \[            [\widehat Q:\widehat E]_\ell              =[\widehat Q:\widehat E]_r=\delta.                 \tag{2} \] Choose lifts b_1,...,b_delta of a residue-field basis. They form a basis on either side. More precisely, \[  v\left(\sum_i b_i e_i\right)=\min_i v(e_i),\qquad  v\left(\sum_i e_i b_i\right)=\min_i v(e_i).                    \tag{3} \] For a nonzero sum, remove its minimum h power and reduce. Residue linear independence forbids cancellation. This proves (3) and independence.  For spanning, first multiply an element by a power of h to give nonnegative valuation. Expand its residue in the chosen basis with coefficients in the residue of Ehat, and lift those coefficients to elements of Ehat of nonnegative valuation. Subtract this finite sum; the remainder has valuation at least one. Repeat after division by h. For each basis element the successive coefficients converge in Ehat. Completeness and (3) give the desired expansion. The same construction on the other side proves both assertions.  No assertion about algebraicity of an arbitrary formal operator coefficient is needed. This is a theorem about the completed division rings, not about finite differential orders.  Consequently every full formal lift of psi has completed division degree delta, without a spatial bound. | DIX-QFL1-S4 | claim | proved / partial | In the exact setting/notation of DIX-QFL1, the named sub-result states:  Let A=K[x_1,...,x_{2n}] in characteristic zero with a constant nondegenerate Poisson matrix J and the corresponding Moyal product. Any compatible finite jet extends; an even jet admits an even extension.  Here is an elementary proof, requiring no assumption that f is invertible.  Put D_i={f_i,-}. The D_i commute by (6). Moreover the identity Df J (Df)^t=J makes Df an invertible matrix over A. The D_i therefore form an A-basis of Der_K(A). Their dual one-forms theta^i are constant linear combinations of df_j, so they are polynomial and closed. The cochain complex of this commuting frame is exactly the polynomial de Rham complex, expressed in the theta basis: \[  (dc)_{ij}=D_i c_j-D_j c_i,\qquad  (dE)_{ijk}=D_iE_{jk}+D_jE_{ki}+D_kE_{ij}.          \tag{8} \] In particular H^1=H^2=0. Explicitly, a closed polynomial p-form whose coefficients are homogeneous of ordinary degree q has primitive i_Euler(alpha)/(q+p), for p>0. Summing its homogeneous pieces gives a polynomial primitive. This uses the original source coordinates and the inverse Jacobian matrix, never an inverse polynomial map f^{-1}.  Suppose the normalized commutators of a compatible jet are J_ij+hbar^m E_ij+O(hbar^{m+1}). Their Jacobi identity at the first remaining order gives dE=0 in (8). Vanishing of H^2 supplies polynomial c_i with dc=-E. Adding hbar^m c_i to every image removes that defect. Induction proves (7); parity follows from the Moyal commutator as before. | [dixmier/dixmier-formal-lifting/PROOF.md](dixmier/dixmier-formal-lifting/PROOF.md): Section Full polynomial symplectic frames are formally unobstructed |
| DIX-QFL1-S5 | claim | proved / partial | In the exact setting/notation of DIX-QFL1, the named sub-result states:  [Baranovsky, Ginzburg, Kaledin and Pecharich, Theorem 1.1.4](https://arxiv.org/html/1403.3493v2) give existence criteria for a line bundle on a smooth closed Lagrangian subvariety to quantize as a complete flat module over a fixed formal quantization. For the graph of (6) in the product with opposite symplectic form, the graph is affine space. Their criterion therefore permits the trivial graph line bundle to quantize. This is consistent with (7), whose regular left module and right action through F give a formal graph bimodule.  This comparison concerns formal deformation quantization. It is not a theorem about a characteristic-zero D-module with a prescribed family of positive-characteristic arithmetic supports. | [dixmier/dixmier-formal-lifting/PROOF.md](dixmier/dixmier-formal-lifting/PROOF.md): Section Comparison with graph quantization |

| DIX-QFL2-S1 | claim | proved / partial | In the exact setting/notation of DIX-QFL2, the named sub-result states:  For a characteristic-zero field K, put R=K[[t]], L=K((t)), and let a(t) be a nonzero element of tR. Its t-adic completion is larger: spatial degrees may grow with t order.  Suppose the images F_i of a formal lift satisfy \[                 \deg_{\rm spatial}F_i\le D  \quad\hbox{for every image and every t coefficient}.       \tag{2} \] There are finitely many spatial monomials of degree <=D, so all F_i belong to the uncompleted algebra (1). They therefore define an endomorphism phi_R of (1). After inverting t, rescaling each p_i by a(t)^{-1} identifies W_L(a) with A_n(L). This rescaling preserves spatial degree. This is the first useful improvement over demanding termination of the formal series. | [dixmier/dixmier-formal-lifting/BOUNDED_REALIZATION.md](dixmier/dixmier-formal-lifting/BOUNDED_REALIZATION.md): Section The algebra that bounded degree supplies |
| DIX-QFL2-S2 | claim | proved / partial | In the exact setting/notation of DIX-QFL2, the named sub-result states:  Assume the commutative reduction \[         f^*:K[x_1,\ldots,p_n]\longrightarrow K[x_1,\ldots,p_n] \] of phi_R is injective. Then \[                          v(\phi_L(g))=v(g).         \tag{3} \]  To prove this, write g=t^m g_0 with g_0 in W_R(a) and nonzero reduction bar(g_0). Reducing phi_R(g_0) gives f^*(bar(g_0)), which is nonzero by injectivity. Thus phi_R(g_0) has valuation zero, proving (3).  If phi_L were surjective, take a finite PBW preimage g_i of each standard generator. Equation (3) gives v(g_i)=0, so every g_i already belongs to W_R(a). Reduction supplies a polynomial preimage of every generator under f^*. Hence f^* is surjective. We have proved \[  \boxed{\quad f^*\text{ injective and not surjective}              \ \Longrightarrow\ \phi_L\text{ not surjective}.\quad} \tag{4} \]  A polynomial symplectic map has invertible Jacobian, hence is dominant and induces an injective polynomial-ring map in characteristic zero. In the commutative example x -> t*x, the generic inverse x/t has a pole and the special reduction is zero. There is no such pole cancellation when f^* is injective. | DIX-QFL2-S3 | claim | proved / partial | In the exact setting/notation of DIX-QFL2, the named sub-result states:  Fix n and D. Write V_e for the spatial polynomials of degree <=e, and put \[                          E=D^{2n-1}. \] For each point m of M_(n,D), substitution through its assignment gives \[        T_m:V_E\longrightarrow V_{DE},\qquad g\mapsto\phi_m(g).  \tag{6} \] Its matrix entries are polynomial in the parameters. | DIX-QFL2-S7 | claim | proved / partial | In the exact setting/notation of DIX-QFL2, the named sub-result states:  The bounded polynomial quantum shear \[                      x\mapsto x,\qquad p\mapsto p+h^2x^2       \tag{10} \] also reduces to the identity at h=0. A word containing j copies of h^2x^2 contributes to its p-order-zero part only with exponents h^(ell+j) x^(3j-ell). Centrality forces 3j-ell divisible by ell. | DIX-QFT1-S2 | claim | open / partial | In the exact setting/notation of DIX-QFT1, the named sub-result states:  After algebraic closure of constants, a finite simple pole has \[                           \chi_h/h=\alpha/(a-c)+\cdots . \] If alpha is an integer, replace the rational frame by (a-c)^alpha times that frame, removing this apparent pole. The resulting gauge is rational. Repeat at every apparent regular pole. Irregular poles remain.  A rational frame change f changes chi_h by -h*(partial_a f)/f. It does not change the reduction in (1): normalize f by a scalar of its h valuation. Its leading rational coefficient is nonzero, so \[                      v_h((\partial_a f)/f)>=0.               \tag{3} \] This also holds after a finite ramified extension of the scalar parameter field. Poles moving to infinity do not invalidate it.  Let the resulting rational coefficient be \[        \widetilde\chi_h=P(a)+B(a)/A(a),\qquad        \deg B<d:=\deg A,\quad \gcd(A,B)=1.                    \tag{4} \] Every remaining regular pole has nonintegral residue and every irregular pole is genuine. We spell out why cleaning is necessary. At a pole of order j>=2, the coefficient B(c) is nonzero. On a finite derivative-of-delta vector the B(c) term has the highest delta-derivative degree, while (a-c)^j*partial_a lowers it. Thus L has no kernel on a delta module, so there is no point-supported quotient. Its formal adjoint has the same nonzero constant term there and excludes point-supported submodules. At a simple pole the corresponding leading coefficient is proportional to alpha-n-1 on the n-th delta derivative; the adjoint replaces alpha by 1-alpha. | DIX-QFT1-S3 | claim | open / partial | In the exact setting/notation of DIX-QFT1, the named sub-result states:  The normal-ordered Fourier operator associated to A*h*partial_a+C is \[  \widehat L=-q A(h\partial_q)-h A'(h\partial_q)                                   +C(h\partial_q).           \tag{6} \] If P in (4) has degree m>=1, then C=AP+B has degree d+m. Every algebraic element of its Picard--Vessiot field is meromorphic and unramified on the affine line, hence rational. Thus its differential Galois group is connected. Finite algebraic base change cannot reduce that connected group or split its irreducible representation. The same argument and finite-coefficient descent were used in QPH1. | DIX-QPH1-S9 | claim | proved / partial | In the exact setting/notation of DIX-QPH1, the named sub-result states:  The quadratic-order proof is not the limit of this construction. Let k be any characteristic-zero constant field, h a nonzero element, and let g(a) in k[a] have arbitrary degree m>=1. Write G'=g and H'=g^2, and use \[        \mathcal F_g=-as^2/8+sG(a)/4-H(a)/8,\qquad        (\mathcal F_g)_a=-(s-g(a))^2/8.                        \tag{16} \] The Fourier module (5) is again left free of rank two over k<q,a>. It has no proper nonzero right-invariant left submodule after q=v^2/2 and after any further finite algebraic coefficient cover. This includes every finite-degree g_h with classical reduction 4a-3ra^2: higher a powers multiplied by arbitrary positive powers of h do not evade this phase-model obstruction.  Here is an all-degree proof independent of QSO1. Over k[a,s] the rank-one polynomial exponential connection is simple: undo its polynomial gradient shift of the derivatives, and a nonzero polynomial ideal stable under both derivatives contains 1. Partial Fourier transformation is an algebra automorphism, so the Fourier module is simple too.  Regard that module instead over k[q,s]. Its operator q raises a degree by 2m with nonzero leading coefficient g_m^2/8; all other terms, including -h*partial_a, have smaller a degree. Thus 1,a,...,a^(2m-1) form a free k[q,s] basis. Multiplication by a and h*partial_s+mathcal F_s give an integrable connection with polynomial matrices on the whole affine (q,s) plane. It has no finite singularities and is generically irreducible.  We use the following elementary characteristic-zero fact. A generically irreducible nonsingular flat algebraic connection on affine space remains irreducible over every finite algebraic extension of its function field. Over C, an algebraic horizontal subspace over such an extension can be transported using a global analytic fundamental matrix: affine space is simply connected and the flat connection has no finite singularities. Its resulting Grassmannian-valued map is single-valued on the entire affine space. Its Plucker-coordinate ratios are algebraic meromorphic functions and have trivial monodromy. They are rational: the normalization of their algebraic function field would otherwise give a connected finite covering with more than one branch over the complement of its branch locus, whereas a single-valued branch is fixed by all monodromy. Connectedness of that covering forces a single branch. The horizontal subspace therefore descends to the original rational function field, contradicting irreducibility. General characteristic zero follows by descent of the finite coefficients to a finitely generated field and an embedding into C. This does not assume regular singularity at infinity. For differential-module and monodromy background see [Singer, Sections3 and6](https://arxiv.org/html/0712.4124). Section6, immediately after Proposition9, gives the same entire-function argument for connectedness in one variable; the affine-plane subspace argument used here is written out above. | [dixmier/dixmier-formal-lifting/QUINTIC_PHASE_AND_BRANCH_OBSTRUCTION.md](dixmier/dixmier-formal-lifting/QUINTIC_PHASE_AND_BRANCH_OBSTRUCTION.md): Section The phase obstruction survives every finite polynomial g deformation |

Replacing v by (s-g)/2 gives the ring K[r,s,a,d,(s-g)^-1]. Commutation with r first removes d. On the remaining ring the Hamiltonian of s is \[                  \{s,-\}=-\frac4{s-g}\partial_a                      \quad\hbox{with r,s held fixed}.     \tag{2} \] Its fraction-field kernel is K(r,s). The intersection K[r,s,a,(s-g)^-1] intersect K(r,s) is exactly K[r,s]: a reduced denominator in K[r,s] would have to divide a power of s-4a+3ra^2. | DIX-QSC1-S2 | claim | proved / partial | In the exact setting/notation of DIX-QSC1, the named sub-result states:  Let A_R be the finite PBW h-Weyl algebra over R0=K[[h]], and Ahat its h-adic completion. Their complete joint centralizer is \[  Bhat=\left\{\sum_{j\ge0}h^j P_j(F_1,F_2):                                   P_j\in K[u_1,u_2]\right\}.                                                                \tag{4} \] Indeed a centralizer element has classical reduction in (3). Subtract its corresponding polynomial in the commuting F_i, divide by h, and repeat. Algebraic independence of R,S makes this representation unique. Conversely every such series commutes with both F_i. In particular Bhat is commutative.  This argument permits arbitrary h-small corrections to both images. It uses no positional normalization, scalar differential order, finite Fourier comparison or prescribed arithmetic support. The finite or generic algebraic centralizer can be strictly smaller than (4), but it is commutative whenever it embeds faithfully there. | DIX-QSC1-S3 | claim | proved / partial | In the exact setting/notation of DIX-QSC1, the named sub-result states:  For a finite idempotent corner e*Mat_s(A_R)*e with e mod h=e11, the completed left module is free of rank one. Its completed corner identifies with Ahat. The finite corner embeds faithfully in its completion, since its matrix coefficients are h-separated. If two right images reduce to R,S, their finite joint centralizer is therefore commutative by (4). No finite conjugating frame is being inferred.  More generally, consider a rank-one torsion-free generic left module P over the Weyl algebra A=A_R tensor K((h)), with a finite h-lattice M whose completion is free of rank one. The same conclusion holds for its generic endomorphism algebra under these explicit hypotheses. Here is the faithfulness argument. An embedding P into A is obtained by a fractional-ideal realization. After clearing h poles on finitely many generators of its lattice M, there is an injection M into A_R. Thus M is h-separated.  Every generic endomorphism of P, multiplied by a sufficiently high power of h, preserves M. It extends to its free completion. If that extension is zero, separatedness makes it zero on M, hence on P. Consequently the generic algebra E=End_A(P)^op embeds faithfully in Ahat[h^-1]. Its centralizer of the two Long right images is commutative by (4).  A partial finite-left module does not automatically meet the rank-one, torsion-free or faithfulness hypotheses. Nor does formal left freeness imply generic left finiteness; QGM1 remains the countercontrol. The carrier consequence uses the stated QMC1 hypotheses and its external generic-projectivity dependency. | [dixmier/dixmier-formal-lifting/LONG_SPECTRAL_CURVATURE_AND_SCALARIZATION.md](dixmier/dixmier-formal-lifting/LONG_SPECTRAL_CURVATURE_AND_SCALARIZATION.md): Section Finite projective carriers retain this commutativity |
| DIX-QSC1-S4 | claim | proved / partial | In the exact setting/notation of DIX-QSC1, the named sub-result states:  Let E be a unital characteristic-zero algebra with central nonzerodivisor h, and fix two commuting elements F1,F2. The parameter ui acts by right multiplication by Fi.  The two commuting monic expressions Fi-ui have the free Koszul resolution. Exactness follows successively by monic division in the central variables, which gives injectivity at each step. Applying Hom(-,M) gives the finite-algebra complex \[  E\xrightarrow{d_0}E^2\xrightarrow{d_1}E,\qquad  d_0(T)=([F_1,T],[F_2,T]),\quad  d_1(A,B)=[F_1,B]-[F_2,A].                                 \tag{6} \] Thus its cohomology computes the spectral self-Ext groups. ## Meridional rank

**Topic scope:** Knot-group representations, branched-cover bounds and explicit sharp families.

**Computed obligation progress:** 5 open.

Finite named equalities, four uniform periodic families and general cover bounds are separate scopes. Compact certificate replays do not replay the retired broad campaign.

The original sixteen rank-four examples lie in the known BJW18 graph-cover family, and the sixteen sharp-five examples are known Montesinos. Global novelty of other seeds/families remains unestablished.

Cover invariants have proved connected-sum formulas under exact hypotheses and proved deficiencies; neither supplies unrestricted meridional-rank additivity or the full MRC.
